mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the next month reduces discount rates applied to corporate earnings forecasts, lowering the present value of future cash flows and thereby driving negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by 0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite sustained FEDFUNDS increases above 4% for 30 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 in the prior month coincides with stronger consumer demand, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns fail to outperform a 200-day moving average baseline during periods of high PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) surprise below expectations triggers a risk-off reaction in equities, generating negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate future inflation easing.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain positive despite CPIAUCSL continuing to decline for 4 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing demand, which reduces corporate earnings visibility and results in negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the three-month INDPRO contraction.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both the 10-year Treasury yield and FEDFUNDS suggest the Fed is maintaining a restrictive stance, compressing equity discount rates and pushing 20-day S&P 500 forward returns to the negative.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative when both proxies show the described relationship.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment benefits applications (PAYEMS) exceeding 10,000 in a month signals weak labor market absorption, lowering consumer confidence and producing negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10,000 in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during such PAYEMS spikes.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly housing starts (HOUST) exceed expectations by 15% for two consecutive months, it indicates resilient housing market momentum that supports optimism in economic growth and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month's value by >15% for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative during the two-month surge in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, the low unemployment rate suggests a tight labor market that elevates equity risk premiums, producing negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive during the three-month UNRATE < 4% streak.
